25. When all these facts are taken into consideration, then it is evident that the cause of altercation was demand of alcohol by the so called Baratis which formed a group of complainant party.
When Pyar Singh had refused to give alcohol then since Baratis were in their own ' Masti' under the influence of alcohol, they started pelting stones on each other.
Rama died at a distance of at least 4 to 6 kms from the place of incident as is evident from the testimonies of Investigating Officer as well as other prosecution witnesses.
Dead body of Rama was recovered from river Tapti.
Prosecution witnesses have admitted that from Davlikhurd the distance of Baghnala is about 2-3 kms and Tapti river is ahead of Baghnala.

Diatom test shows that death was due to drowning.
It is not a case of dead body being thrown in a waterbody.

sentences.text: , taking this fact into consideration that witnesses have admitted that they were informed by the police that how the story is to be built coupled with the fact that Investigation Officer did not deem it proper to cause Test Identification Parade of accused persons despite the fact that prosecution witnesses admitted that they had visited village Davalikhurd for the first time and the accused persons were not known to them especially when Bhuruji (PW-1) admits that outside the court police personnel had shown him the accused persons, the name of Subhash is not mentioned in the FIR.

It is humanly impossible to recollect names and faces after six months of the incident especially when the accused persons were not previously acquainted to the complainant party, present appears to be a case of false implication and, therefore, when all the facts of the case are taken into consideration then it is evident that present being a case based on surmises and conjectures, benefit of doubt is required to be extended in favour of the accused persons.
Their conviction cannot be sustained in the eyes of law.

Hence,
impugned judgment of conviction dated 25.02.2016 passed by learned First Additional Sessions Judge, Burhanpur (M.P.) in S.T. No.45/2011, is hereby set aside and the appellants are acquitted from all the charges levelled against them.

25. When all these facts are taken into consideration, then it is evident that the cause of altercation was demand of alcohol by the so called Baratis which formed a group of complainant party.
When Pyar Singh had refused to give alcohol then since Baratis were in their own ' Masti' under the influence of alcohol, they started pelting stones on each other.
Rama died at a distance of at least 4 to 6 kms from the place of incident as is evident from the testimonies of Investigating Officer as well as other prosecution witnesses.
Dead body of Rama was recovered from river Tapti.
Prosecution witnesses have admitted that from Davlikhurd the distance of Baghnala is about 2-3 kms and Tapti river is ahead of Baghnala.
They have admitted that the terrain is rocky around Tapti river.
Bhuruji (PW-1) admitted that Rama had also fallen before climbing the rock and soon after climbing the rock he had fallen in riverbed.
Diatom test shows that death was due to drowning.
It is not a case of dead body being thrown in a waterbody.

7 at the time of the incident i.e. about 5-5.30 p.m.; and secondly
, taking this fact into consideration that witnesses have admitted that they were informed by the police that how the story is to be built coupled with the fact that Investigation Officer did not deem it proper to cause Test Identification Parade of accused persons despite the fact that prosecution witnesses admitted that they had visited village Davalikhurd for the first time and the accused persons were not known to them especially when Bhuruji (PW-1) admits that outside the court police personnel had shown him the accused persons, the name of Subhash is not mentioned in the FIR.
It is humanly impossible to recollect names and faces after six months of the incident especially when the accused persons were not previously acquainted to the complainant party, present appears to be a case of false implication and, therefore, when all the facts of the case are taken into consideration then it is evident that present being a case based on surmises and conjectures, benefit of doubt is required to be extended in favour of the accused persons.
Their conviction cannot be sustained in the eyes of law.
